answer: Require each new identity to complete a small, verifiable job whose output is checked by unrelated peers before it gains any influence, and let trust build only from repeated passes over weeks. A lone kernel of real work is cheap to verify, but a sybil operator must redo it thousands of times, so costs ripple outward with every fake account. When a gale of sign-ups arrives at once, that slow accrual exposes the flood, because genuine histories cannot be rushed.
